faq.q: What is a before and after video maker?
faq.a: A tool that builds a short ad of a change, from a product photo, a note you type, or a product link. The clip includes a script, a presenter, a voice, captions, and the edit. Show a change your product really makes to an item or the space around it, not a health, skin, or body result.

faq.q: How do I make a before and after video?
faq.a: Add a product link or a photo, name the start and the result, then download or publish. You can edit the script, the captions, and the music in the built-in editor before it goes out.

faq.q: Which maker should I use for this kind of ad?
faq.a: Use AIVideosUGC when you want several versions from photos or links you already have. The sizes fit TikTok, Reels, Shorts, and Meta.

faq.q: Is a before and after video free to make?
faq.a: No. Plans start at $24.50 a month. Credits pay for each video: 24 for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. You see the cost before it starts. If the video fails, the credits come back.
Yes. Finished clips can run as paid ads or ordinary posts, and they have no watermark.

faq.q: Which sizes can I publish, and where?
faq.a: Choose a size: 9:16 (tall), 1:1 (square), 16:9 (wide), 4:3 (a bit wide), or 3:4 (a bit tall). You can also switch the spoken line and the captions to another language, and pick a matching voice. Send the file to TikTok or Meta from the editor, or download it.

faq.q: Can I make one for every product at once?
faq.a: Yes. Add a group of photos or product links and get a clip for each item. Every clip spends its own credits. A store can also send photos through an API, a connection for its own software, and get the clips back.

faq.q: Will this do as well as filming the change?
faq.a: Results vary by product and audience. Many shops use these clips to try opening lines quickly. They still film a main ad when they want a real shoot.

faq.q: Will TikTok or Meta reject an AI before and after ad?
faq.a: Check the current rule before you spend more on ads. Some ad spots ask you to label the clip when it could look like a real customer. Anyone on screen is a generated presenter, not a buyer.
